Source: World Bank Commodity Markets Outlook, Commodity Price Data (The
Pink Sheet), `CMO-Historical-Data-Annual.xlsx`, release of 2026-09-02,
downloaded 2026-10-10 (`_data/raw/worldbank/`), sheet Annual Prices (Real),
2010 US dollars deflated by the MUV index.
Pipeline script: `_scripts/03-controls-prices.R` (weights from
`03-controls-agro.R`).
Interim outputs: `_data/interim/prices_real_normalized_2000_2020.rds`,
`prices_index_2000_2020.rds`.
Equivalence with the recovered panel is not checked here (the notebook never
reads `_data/reference/`); the `compare_outputs` report lives in the phase 1
script 03 commit message and in the decision entries it cites.

```{r setup}
#| include: false
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(tidyverse)
  library(readxl)
})
options(width = 110)
```

```{r read}
pink_raw <- read_excel("_data/raw/worldbank/CMO-Historical-Data-Annual.xlsx",
                       sheet = "Annual Prices (Real)", col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text",
                       .name_repair = "minimal")
prices_norm <- read_rds("_data/interim/prices_real_normalized_2000_2020.rds")
prices_index <- read_rds("_data/interim/prices_index_2000_2020.rds")
weights <- read_rds("_data/interim/pam_ppm_weights_base_2000_2002.rds")
sample_geo <- read_rds("_data/interim/mapbiomas_deforestation_amz_1987_2023.rds") %>%
  distinct(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation)
```

## Q1. What is the layout and the release of the workbook?

```{r q1-layout}
excel_sheets("_data/raw/worldbank/CMO-Historical-Data-Annual.xlsx")
pink_raw[1:4, 1]
series <- c("Soybeans", "Maize", "Rice, Thai 5%", "Cotton, A Index", "Beef")
idx <- match(series, str_trim(unlist(pink_raw[7, ])))
tibble(series, column = idx, unit = str_trim(unlist(pink_raw[8, idx])),
       first_year = pink_raw[[1]][9], last_year = pink_raw[[1]][nrow(pink_raw)])
```

**Finding.** The sheet keeps the legacy layout: commodity names on row 7,
units on row 8, data from row 9 (1960) to 2025, year in the first column.
The release header reads "Updated on September 02, 2026". The five series
are present under their legacy names, soy, maize and rice in dollars per
tonne, cotton and beef per kilogram.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-a (release accepted; the real series are
recomputed at each MUV revision, so the indices drift from the lost
release by a fraction of a percent).
**Assertion.** `03-controls-prices.R`, raw-state block (names, units,
first year, complete 2000-2020).

## Q2. How do the normalised real series move over 2000-2020?

```{r q2-plot}
#| fig-height: 4
prices_norm %>%
  pivot_longer(-year, names_to = "commodity", values_to = "index") %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, index, colour = commodity)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Real price, 2000 = 1", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
prices_norm %>% filter(year %in% c(2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020))
```

**Finding.** All five series equal 1 in 2000 by construction; rice peaks
at 2.5 in 2008, maize at 2.4 and soy at 2.0 in 2012, cotton at 1.8 in
2011 before returning to its base, and beef climbs steadily to twice its
2000 level by 2019-2020.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-h.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-prices.R`, output block (2000 values equal 1,
positive series).

## Q3. Is the index anchored to 1 in 2000 for both crop and cattle?

```{r q3-anchor}
prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, year == 2000) %>%
  summarise(across(c(price_index_crop, price_index_cattle),
                   list(n_na = ~ sum(is.na(.x)), min = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                        p50 = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE), max = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("index", "stat"),
               names_pattern = "(price_index_[a-z]+)_(n_na|min|p50|max)$") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = stat, values_from = value)
prices_index %>% filter(geocode == "1100015", year %in% 2000:2002) %>%
  left_join(weights, by = "geocode") %>%
  select(year, price_index_crop, price_index_cattle, cattle_weight)
```

**Finding.** Neither index is 1 in 2000. The crop index in 2000 equals the
municipality's total base-window crop share (a few hundredths for most of
the sample) and the cattle index equals its base-window density (tens of
heads per km2), because the weights do not sum to one and normalisation
ran before the join.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-05-p, closed by D-2026-10-23-a (phase 2, step 2.4,
2026-10-23): the 2000 value is the municipality's base-window exposure and
is meant to be; the world series, not the index, are normalised to
2000 = 1, and the level is absorbed by municipality fixed effects. No
anchoring (Q6 shows what it would do).
**Assertion.** none; the exposure level is documented, not constrained.

## Q4. Are the scales comparable?

```{r q4-scales}
prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  pivot_longer(starts_with("price_index"), names_to = "index", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(index) %>%
  summarise(n_na = sum(is.na(value)), min = min(value, na.rm = TRUE), p50 = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            max = max(value, na.rm = TRUE), sd = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
```

**Finding.** The cattle index is three orders of magnitude larger than the
crop index and both carry the cross-sectional scale of the weights (a
share of the territory against heads per km²), so the two coefficients
are not comparable in raw units; script 04 standardises them. The scale
difference is the unit of the exposures, not an error, and is left as is
(D-2026-10-23-a); a pasture-share exposure for cattle would put both on
the 0-1 scale (D-2026-10-23-c, Q7).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-a; D-2026-10-23-c open.

## Q5. Which municipalities have a zero or missing index, and why?

```{r q5-missing}
prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode, year == 2000,
         is.na(price_index_crop) | price_index_crop == 0 | is.na(price_index_cattle)) %>%
  left_join(weights, by = "geocode") %>%
  left_join(sample_geo, by = "geocode") %>%
  select(geocode, municipality, state_abbreviation, price_index_crop, price_index_cattle,
         starts_with("crop_w_"), cattle_weight)
```

**Finding.** Nine sample municipalities have a zero or missing index in
2000. Five (Barcelos, Santa Isabel do Rio Negro and Uarini in Amazonas,
Belém and Marituba in Pará) planted none of the four crops in 2000-2002,
so their crop index is a true zero, a constant absorbed by the
municipality effect. Ipiranga do Norte, Itanhangá and Mojuí dos Campos
have no crop index (NA since phase 2 step 2.4; 0 in phase 1, when the
weighted sum dropped their four NA weights) because they have no PAM
value in the window, and no cattle index, their density weight being NA.
Santa Cruz do Arari has no crop index, having no PAM series, and keeps
its cattle index through the full join of the two indices.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-10-h (true zero for an empty basket);
D-2026-10-23-b (NA for an all-NA window); D-2026-10-10-i (Santa Cruz do
Arari); task 1.8 for the remaining codings of absence.
**Assertion.** `03-controls-prices.R`, output block (crop index NA exactly
for municipalities whose four weights are missing; lag NA in 2000 or where
the index is NA).

## Q6. What would anchoring each index at 2000 = 1 within the municipality do?

Task 1.3 planned to divide each municipality's index by its own 2000
value (D-2026-10-05-p). The procedure was implemented on the step 2.4
branch and reversed; this section keeps the evidence. What is checked:
the anchored values recomputed here for the sample, the municipalities
that would have no anchor, the cross-sectional range of the anchored
cattle index within a year, and the split of the anchored crop index's
variance between years and within years.

```{r q6-anchored}
anchored <- prices_index %>%
  filter(geocode %in% sample_geo$geocode) %>%
  group_by(geocode) %>%
  mutate(crop_base = price_index_crop[year == 2000],
         cattle_base = price_index_cattle[year == 2000],
         crop_a = if_else(crop_base > 0, price_index_crop / crop_base, NA_real_),
         cattle_a = if_else(cattle_base > 0, price_index_cattle / cattle_base, NA_real_)) %>%
  ungroup()
anchored %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(crop_mean = mean(crop_a, na.rm = TRUE),
            crop_sd_within_year = sd(crop_a, na.rm = TRUE),
            cattle_mean = mean(cattle_a, na.rm = TRUE),
            cattle_range_within_year = diff(range(cattle_a, na.rm = TRUE)),
            n_munic_no_crop_anchor = sum(is.na(crop_a)),
            n_munic_no_cattle_anchor = sum(is.na(cattle_a)),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(across(-year, ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2000, 2004, 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020))
anchored %>%
  filter(!is.na(crop_a)) %>%
  mutate(year_mean = ave(crop_a, year)) %>%
  summarise(between_year_sd = round(sd(year_mean), 3),
            within_year_sd = round(sd(crop_a - year_mean), 3))
```

**Finding.** Anchoring cancels the exposure. The cattle index, built on
one commodity, becomes the relative beef price in every municipality
with a herd (zero range within a year), a pure year series that year
effects absorb; the nine municipalities of the 503 with a zero or missing
2000 crop value (eight in the sample panel, Mojuí dos Campos being
dropped) and the six with a zero or missing cattle value (five) would
have no anchor and become NA. The anchored crop index keeps only the crop-mix
variation: a within-year sd of about 0.07 against a between-year sd of
about 0.38, intensity having cancelled. The exposure form that script 03
produces is the shift-share control the design asks for, and its 2000
level is absorbed by the municipality effect.
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-a: no anchoring; D-2026-10-05-p closed by
reinterpretation.
**Assertion.** none; the procedure was rejected.

## Q7. Can the cattle exposure be expressed as a pasture share from the raw layer?

A 2000-2002 pasture share of the territory would put the cattle exposure
on the 0-1 scale of the crop shares. What is checked: whether the
MapBiomas workbook in the raw layer carries land-cover classes.

```{r q7-sheets}
readxl::excel_sheets("_data/raw/mapbiomas/mapbiomas_munic.xlsx")
```

**Finding.** The workbook is the deforestation and secondary-vegetation
module only: one data sheet (`DEF_SECVEG`, four transition names, see
`mapbiomas.qmd` Q1), its pivot, a README and metadata; no land-cover
class, so no pasture area. A pasture share needs a new acquisition
(MapBiomas Collection 9 land-cover statistics by municipality, class 15,
or the Censo Agropecuário 2006 pasture area).
**Decision.** D-2026-10-23-c, open, reserved to the author.
**Assertion.** none.
